documents.instruction: The three-part mental model (identities and aliases declare, capabilities and subscriptions pay, bounded dispatch records) must stay true to the ingress in src/core/server.rs, the dispatch bounds in src/subscription_dispatch/dispatch.rs, and the product boundaries stated in README.md and CORE.md.

Every command, flag, endpoint, and pasted output on the happy path must match the CLI in src/main.rs, the routes in src/core/server.rs, and the launcher contract in scripts/start-with-skarbiec.sh, including the exact bare-serve refusal sentence.

The ownership boundaries, request-path pipeline, trust-boundary table, /health-versus-/readyz evidence rule, and state-on-disk table must track src/core/server.rs (transport guard, routers, readyz probes), src/gateway (credential seams), and the state paths the process actually writes.

All 19 routes with their request and response shapes, status codes, and quoted error bodies must match the handlers and error_response/api_error mapping in src/core/server.rs and the dialect translation in src/core/wire.rs.

Every subcommand, flag, default, exit code, and pasted output must match the clap definitions and match arms in src/main.rs and the verdict/report shapes in src/subscription_dispatch/pool.rs and quality.rs.
The client error-code table must match api_error in src/core/server.rs, and the operator envelope tables (failure points, kind-to-fleet-code mapping) must match src/core/failure.rs exactly.
Every variable name, default, and reader location must correspond to an env read in src/ or a launcher input in scripts/start-with-skarbiec.sh; a knob that no code reads must not be listed.

Every symptom entry quotes an error sentence that exists verbatim in src/ (readyz reasons, dispatch refusals, refresh verdict details, routes-file guards, transport guard) and pairs it with the repair the code implies; no invented strings.

Every console block is genuinely captured from a running gateway against the loopback stub in docs/examples/stub-provider.py; re-execute the sequence and re-paste when the routes, error bodies, or provider override validation change.

Every console block is genuinely captured (pool report, empty-pool refresh, journal record, signed listing, admin surface); re-execute and re-paste when the pool report shape, refresh verdict, journal schema, or HMAC contract changes.
The identity fields, bearer resolution order, five-second verdict cache, special brama-desktop/brama-user identities, and quoted 401/403 refusals must match the ingress auth in src/core/server.rs.
The four-part model-name vocabulary, required alias set, routes-file schema, and every quoted guard sentence must match src/core/server.rs and src/core/inference_routes.rs verbatim.

The purpose/resource/agent shape, issue limits, read-grant fallback, standalone in-memory map, and final-use invariants must match src/gateway/broker.rs, including the coordinate formats provider:<slug> and provider:<slug>:<slug>.
The 23-descriptor table, pinned default models, base-URL override validation sentences, plan-usage endpoints, and timeout/size bounds must match src/providers/adapter.rs exactly.

The vault-tag discovery contract, four pool states, last_redeem_error precedence, ledger semantics, block durations, definitive-refusal word list, and donation/retirement rules must match the named source files.

The HMAC message format, central agent list, pool-payment table, attempt bounds (2 credentials, 3 selector models), pinning rules, and every quoted refusal sentence must match src/subscription_dispatch/dispatch.rs and src/crypto/hmac_auth.rs.
The nine failure points and four impact statements must match the constants in src/core/failure.rs verbatim, and the example envelope must remain one genuinely captured from a running gateway.
The envelope fields, kind-to-fleet-code table, prefix classification rule, and rendering/secret constraints must match src/core/failure.rs and the wisent-errors derivation it delegates to.
The index must list exactly the scripts present in docs/examples/ with their env knobs and cost statements, and every claim about what a script exercises must match the script body.

The stub must keep speaking the OpenAI chat shape the openai adapter consumes (models list, chat.completion, chat.completion.chunk SSE with [DONE], 401 and 429 error bodies) so the walkthrough captures stay reproducible.

The HMAC computation must stay byte-compatible with verify_agent_hmac in src/crypto/hmac_auth.rs: HMAC-SHA256 hex over {agent}:{timestamp}:{body_sha256_hex} with the empty string for a bodyless GET and a ±300-second window.
The launch sequence must keep matching brama serve --local-credentials-stdin (JSON map over stdin, zeroized) and the loopback-only BRAMA_PROVIDER_OPENAI_BASE_URL override validation.
The script must keep encoding the evidence rule: /health is liveness only (dependencies not_probed) and /readyz is the readiness verdict whose 503 reason names the failing half.

The script must keep to the read-only pool surfaces (brama subscriptions list, GET /v1/admin/subscription-pool) and its output expectations must match the pool report shape in src/subscription_dispatch/pool.rs.
